correctness.rationale: Let P_t be the round-t partition; the claimed depth is the first t with P_t=P_{t+1}. Regular degree and exactly h neighbours in layer h−1 give the frontier induction: at round t the entire layer t has one colour, the higher layers have a separate common colour, and earlier layers stay separated. At round two, the distance-one class splits by the within-layer neighbour count q−2. At distance h≥2, the multiset of deletion profiles contains j_q copies of j−e_q; summing gives (h−1)j, so it distinguishes every profile in round h+1 once the previous layer is resolved. The top layer has only one profile. Equal-size coordinate permutations and root-symbol-fixing alphabet permutations act transitively on each profile, so profiles cannot split and are exactly the eventual orbits. The frontier proves both lower bounds: in a homogeneous product the last two layers are still merged at round k−2 if k≥2, and in a mixed product the layer k−1 is monochromatic at round k−1 despite different profiles obtained by omitting different sizes. For k=1 the initial partition is already stable. The class cardinalities follow by choosing the changed coordinates and their nonroot symbols. The supplied code and its recorded output are consistent finite corroboration; no run was needed for this general proof.
residual_risks: The proof and tests concern synchronous counting refinement with a single marked root, not other schedules or initial colourings.
